text: Da Derga is an Irish god or hero whose name means "the red god". Some texts give the name Úa Dergae, "the nephew of the red goddess". His hostel serves as the setting for a key Irish story about kingship. As the king of Tara, Conaire, arrives at the hostel on Samhain, he breaks a series of sacred vows. Those vows are called geis. A hag demands entrance to the hostel, and Conaire refuses her. The hag stands on one leg like a crane and curses him. Conaire then develops a thirst that no water in Ireland can quench, and he dies of it. Da Derga makes no move to help him, which implies he agrees with the punishment. The point of the story is the punishment of a king who fails his vows to the earth goddess. If Da Derga is the nephew of the red goddess, he may connect to Medb or Flaith, goddesses of sovereignty. If he is the red god, he may belong to the otherworld, since red is linked to that realm. His character is thin. He plays little role in the tale named for him.
objective: Document Da Derga, the Irish red god whose hostel hosts the death of King Conaire.
key_results: Record Da Derga as the Irish red god, also named Úa Dergae.
Document Conaire's death from an unquenchable thirst after breaking his geis at Samhain.
Note the link between Da Derga and goddesses of sovereignty such as Medb.
Note that red links Da Derga to the otherworld.
